request.spec:
A button on each person's row downloads their statement as a CSV file: a header line
number,date,amount,figure,status then one line per claim of theirs bound by their last statement,
oldest first, with the bound figure as the claim shows it.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A button on each person's row downloads their statement as a CSV file: a header line
number,date,amount,figure,status then one line per claim of theirs bound by their last statement,
oldest first, with the bound figure as the claim shows it.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Each person's row now has an "Export statement (CSV)" button (`data-testid="person-export-statement"`) that downloads `statement.csv`. All 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

The file starts with the header `number,date,amount,figure,status`. After that comes one line for each of the person's claims bound by their last statement, oldest first. The figure is the one the claim's row shows: a settled claim's settled amount, otherwise the figure the statement fixed. If no statement has been taken yet, the file holds just the header.

This needed no server or database change. The screen already loads each claim with whether it is bound and its bound figure. A claim stays bound when it is settled, so a settled claim stays in the export with the figure its statement gave it, as the test expects.

The only file changed is `src/main/frontend/src/app/features/people/people.ts`, which has the new button and its `exportStatement()` method. The method uses the same CSV download helper and figure calculation as the existing "Export claims" button.
